record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Fix x0 in the open unit interval. Characterize all functions delta:[0,1] -> [0,1] for which there exists a bivariate copula C such that C(x,x)=delta(x) for every x in [0,1] and C is linear on each segment connecting the diagonal point (x0,x0) to the corner points (1,0) and (0,1). Within this class, construct pointwise maximal and pointwise minimal copulas when they exist.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I=[0,1]$. A bivariate copula is a function $C:I^2\to I$ such that (i) $C(x,0)=C(0,x)=0$ and $C(x,1)=C(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in I$, and (ii) $C$ is 2-increasing, i.e. $C(x_2,y_2)-C(x_2,y_1)-C(x_1,y_2)+C(x_1,y_1)\ge 0$ for all $0\le x_1\le x_2\le 1$ and $0\le y_1\le y_2\le 1$. The diagonal section of $C$ is the function $\delta_C:I\to I$ defined by $\delta_C(x)=C(x,x)$.

Fix a point $x_0\in(0,1)$. Consider the class $\mathcal{C}_{x_0}$ of all bivariate copulas $C$ with the property that $C$ is affine (linear) on each segment joining the point $(x_0,x_0)$ to the corner $(1,0)$ and on each segment joining $(x_0,x_0)$ to the corner $(0,1)$, i.e. on the two families of line segments inside $I^2$ obtained by joining $(x_0,x_0)$ with points of the edges $\{(x,0):x\in I\}\cup\{(1,y):y\in I\}$ and $\{(0,y):y\in I\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in I\}$ that pass through $(x_0,x_0)$.

(a) Give a complete characterization of those functions $\delta:I\to I$ for which there exists $C\in\mathcal{C}_{x_0}$ with $\delta_C=\delta$.

(b) For each admissible diagonal $\delta$, determine whether there exist pointwise maximal and pointwise minimal copulas in the subclass $\{C\in\mathcal{C}_{x_0}:\delta_C=\delta\}$, and if so construct them explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up work "A note on biconic copulas" (Kybernetika, 2011) explicitly studies the class of biconic copulas — those that are linear on segments joining a fixed diagonal point $(x_0,x_0)$ with the corners $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ — and proves a characterization theorem of admissible diagonal sections together with extreme constructions. Subsequent papers (e.g., on biconic aggregation functions with a given diagonal section, and on extreme semilinear copulas) extend and confirm this characterization, so the problem appears to be solved.

status_evidence.title: A note on biconic copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes the class of biconic copulas via their diagonal sections, using a characterization through Dini derivatives.
status_evidence.claim: This paper provides the characterization of diagonals of biconic copulas with apex (x_0,x_0).

status_evidence.title: Biconic aggregation functions with a given diagonal or opposite diagonal section
status_evidence.snippet: Biconic aggregation functions constructed by linear interpolation on segments connecting the diagonal of the unit square and the points (0,1) and (1,0).
status_evidence.claim: Construction and characterization of biconic functions with prescribed diagonal section is established.
